title: South Korean Economy Tops Growth Projections on $148B Chip Export Surge
summary:
Real gross domestic income in South Korea climbed 18.8% in the third quarter, the fastest increase for the measure in nearly 49 years, driven by a spike in demand for chips used in artificial intelligence. Preliminary data from the Bank of Korea show the economy grew 1.0% from the previous quarter, surpassing the central bank's own forecast of 0.3% and an analyst poll estimate of 0.7%.

The expansion was largely fueled by semiconductor exports, which jumped 218.7% from a year ago to $148 billion. While annual gross domestic product grew 3.4% in the July-September period, John Bromhead, a senior economist at Moody's Analytics, cautioned that the growth is heavily concentrated in the chip sector, leaving the economy exposed if global AI spending slows.
